questions.q: A student adds metals X, Y and Z to dilute acid and to each other's sulfate solutions (data on the sheet). (a) Order X, Y, Z [2]. (b) Write a balanced equation for Y with copper(II) sulfate if Y is zinc [2]. (c) Identify the species oxidised and explain [3].
questions.a: (a) from the data: Y > X > Z (2); (b) Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (2); (c) zinc oxidised (1), loses two electrons (1), to form Zn²⁺ (1)
questions.model: Teacher reads the data table and ranks the most reactive metal first.

questions.q: Explain why the rust on a car worsens near the sea.
questions.a: Salt water speeds up rusting (1) because dissolved ions increase the rate of the redox reaction (1)

questions.q: Write the half equations for Fe + CuSO₄.
Explain why zinc protects iron even when a galvanised coating is scratched.
questions.a: Zinc is more reactive than iron (1); zinc is oxidised/loses electrons instead of iron (1); iron does not rust: sacrificial protection (1)
questions.model: Compare reactivity: zinc above iron. More reactive is oxidised first. So zinc corrodes and iron is protected.
